title: Shoryuken configuration
markdownDescription:
Configuration for Shoryuken, a super-efficient AWS SQS thread-based message processor for Ruby.

Shoryuken allows you to process messages from multiple SQS queues concurrently with configurable load balancing and polling strategies.

Supports ERB templating for dynamic configuration values.

[Shoryuken Documentation](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki)

queues.markdownDescription:
List of SQS queues to process.

A single Shoryuken process can consume from multiple queues. You can specify:
- **Queue names:** `["queue1", "queue2"]`
- **Queue URLs:** `["https://sqs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/000/queue1"]`
- **Queue ARNs:** `["arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:queue1"]`

**Load balancing:** Use `[queue_name, weight]` syntax to control fetch frequency:
```yaml
queues:
  - [queue1, 8]  # Fetch 8 times per cycle
  - [queue2, 4]  # Fetch 4 times per cycle
  - [queue3, 1]  # Fetch 1 time per cycle
```

Each fetch can retrieve up to 10 messages (AWS SQS limit).

Queues listed here belong to the `default` processing group. Use `groups` to process other queues with their own settings.

[Queues Documentation](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options#queues)

polling_strategy.markdownDescription:
Polling strategy used to pick which queue to fetch from next.

Default: `WeightedRoundRobin`

- `WeightedRoundRobin` - cycles through queues according to their weights, pausing empty queues for `delay` seconds.
- `StrictPriority` - keeps fetching from the highest priority queue until it is empty before trying the next one.

Any other value is resolved as the name of a custom polling strategy class.

[Polling Strategies Documentation](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Polling-strategies)
markdownEnumDescriptions: Cycle through queues according to their weights (default).
Fetch from the highest priority queue until it is empty, then the next.

logfile.markdownDescription:
Path to the log file.

Default: STDOUT

Example: `./shoryuken.log`

**CLI equivalent:** `-L, --logfile PATH`

[Shoryuken Options](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options)

pidfile.markdownDescription:
Path to the PID file.

Useful for process management and deployments.

Example: `./shoryuken.pid`

**CLI equivalent:** `-P, --pidfile PATH`

[Shoryuken Options](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options)

daemon.markdownDescription:
Run Shoryuken as a daemon in the background.

Default: `false`

When daemonized, STDOUT and STDERR are redirected to `logfile`, so a `logfile` should be set.

**CLI equivalent:** `-d, --daemon`

[Shoryuken Options](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options)

verbose.markdownDescription:
Enable verbose (`DEBUG` level) logging.

Default: `false`

**CLI equivalent:** `-v, --verbose`

[Shoryuken Options](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options)

require.markdownDescription:
Path to a file, or a directory of workers, to require before starting.

When a directory is given, every `*.rb` file within it (recursively) is required.

Example: `./app/workers`

**CLI equivalent:** `-r, --require PATH`

[Shoryuken Options](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options)

groups.markdownDescription:
Processing groups, each with its own queues, concurrency, delay and polling strategy.

Queues in different groups are fetched independently, so a busy queue in one group does not delay fetching from queues in another.

Example:
```yaml
groups:
  group1:
    concurrency: 1
    queues:
      - queue1
  group2:
    concurrency: 10
    delay: 10
    polling_strategy: StrictPriority
    queues:
      - queue2
      - queue3
```

[Processing Groups Documentation](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Processing-Groups)

additionalProperties.markdownDescription: A processing group. Settings not set here fall back to the top-level values.

concurrency.markdownDescription:
Number of threads available for processing messages from this group.

Defaults to the top-level `concurrency`.

delay.markdownDescription:
Number of seconds to pause fetching from an empty queue in this group.

Defaults to the top-level `delay`.

Number of seconds to pause fetching from an empty queue.

Default: `0`

When Shoryuken fetches from a queue and finds no messages, it will pause fetching from that queue for this many seconds.

**Cost vs. Speed tradeoff:**
- `delay: 0` - Fetch continuously (faster message processing, higher AWS costs)
- `delay: 25` - Pause 25 seconds when empty (lower costs, slower to pick up new messages)

Example:
```yaml
delay: 25
queues:
  - queue1
  - queue2
```

If `queue1` is empty, Shoryuken pauses fetching from `queue1` for 25 seconds but continues fetching from `queue2`.

[AWS SQS Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/sqs/pricing/) | [Delay Documentation](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options#delay)

concurrency.markdownDescription:
Number of threads available for processing messages concurrently.

Default: `25`

**Important:** 
- Be careful increasing this value to avoid overwhelming your system with I/O operations
- When using databases (ActiveRecord) or connection pools, set the pool size >= concurrency
- Higher concurrency = more memory usage

Example with environment variable:
```yaml
concurrency: <%= ENV.fetch('SHORYUKEN_CONCURRENCY', 25) %>
```

In Rails `database.yml`:
```yaml
production:
  pool: <%= ENV.fetch('SHORYUKEN_CONCURRENCY', 25) %>
```

[Concurrency Documentation](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options#concurrency)

timeout.markdownDescription:
Number of seconds to wait for in-flight workers to finish when shutting down, before they are forcibly killed.

Default: `8`

**CLI equivalent:** `-t, --timeout NUM`

[Shoryuken Options](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Shoryuken-options)

thread_priority.markdownDescription:
Ruby thread priority used for the threads that dispatch work to processors.

Default: `-1`

See [`Thread#priority`](https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/Thread.html#method-i-priority).

aws.markdownDescription:
Options passed to `Aws::SQS::Client.new` when Shoryuken creates its default SQS client.

Example:
```yaml
aws:
  region: us-east-1
```

AWS credentials are usually better configured outside Shoryuken (environment variables, `~/.aws/credentials`, instance profiles, or `Shoryuken.sqs_client = ...` in Ruby).

[Configure the AWS Client](https://github.com/ruby-shoryuken/shoryuken/wiki/Configure-the-AWS-Client) | [Aws::SQS::Client options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-ruby/v3/api/Aws/SQS/Client.html#initialize-instance_method)
